newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Private firm opens first agro centre in Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Private firm opens first agro centre in Ukraine.

text.p: Kyiv-Atlantic, a U.S.-Ukraine joint venture, opened a $25 million agricultural processing centre on Friday, the first in the former Soviet republic where most of the farm sector is still heavily state-controlled.
The Kyiv-Atlantic Ukraine centre, 120 kilometres south of the capital Kiev, consists of a 38,000-tonne grain elevator, feed mill and oil processing plant.
"We believe in Ukraine, we believe in the agricultural potential of Ukraine, we believe in the market of Ukraine," president David Sweere said at the opening.

Sweere said Kyiv Atlantic, which received funding of about $8 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, and the U.S. government planned to produce and bottle cooking oil and would also open a farm equipment centre.
He added the company also planned to open smaller centres in other regions of Ukraine, which was the breadbasket of the former Soviet Union.

Company plans called for purchasing and processing grain from farms within a 160-kilometre radius around Myronivka, a traditional grain-producing area. Thirteen regional farms also purchased shares in Kyiv-Atlantic.
Ukraine has predicted a grain harvest of about 37 million tonnes this year, compared to 25.4 million from last year's drought-hit harvest.
